summary: Run 1 (taxi-scenario-basic) reads as a credible owner-driver set of accounts: fares £36,000, fuel £3,600, road tax/insurance £1,380, £8,000 vehicle capitalised with £1,120 WDA, and tax/NI of £4,147 on a £28,520 profit. Run 2 (SP Sixty Driving) also holds up on totals, but the profit & loss cost of sales of £4,896 does not agree with the vehicle cost lines it is said to be built from (£2,708 + £580 + £1,580 + £28 = £4,896 only if the £28 allowance is included, which it is — so that reconciles), while the SA103S "net profit for tax calc" of £31,612 is £172 below the P&L net profit of £31,784 with nothing in the report explaining the difference. That unexplained step is a note, not a blocker, so both runs pass.

concerns.figure: SA103S Net profit for tax calc 31,612 vs P&L Net Profit 31,784 (SE Short D106 / Profit & Loss B23)
concerns.where: Run taxi-scenario-sp-sixty, Self Assessment (SA103S) and Profit & Loss Account
concerns.why: In run 1 the SA103S profit for tax equals the P&L net profit exactly (28,520 both). In run 2 it is 172 lower, and the report gives no adjustment line to account for the step. The 200 capitalised purchase and the 28 capital allowance are the likely cause (31,812 - 200 = 31,612), which would mean the capitalised asset is being deducted again in the tax figure. Worth a look at SE Short D106 and the feeding cells, though the amount is immaterial and every deterministic tie-out passed.

An owner-driver doing 12 months of fares with 3,600 of fuel records no repairs or servicing at all. The purchase journal genuinely has no 'r' coded entries so the sheet is faithful to its input, but a full year of taxi work with zero maintenance spend is an unusual fact pattern rather than a spreadsheet fault.

Fuel is only about 7% of fares for a private hire driver, where 15-25% would be more typical. It matches the journal code d exactly so nothing has been lost in the workbook, but the underlying scenario looks fuel-light for the level of fares.

concerns.figure: New Asset Cost (Vehicle under £12,000) 200, Fixed Assets D47
concerns.why: The 200 of code f spend is the dashcam/signage described in the scenario, but it lands on a row labelled as a motor vehicle under 12,000 and attracts a 14% vehicle WDA rather than being pooled as plant. The classification is a presentational quirk of the schedule, not an arithmetic error, and the 28 allowance ties to the P&L.
